OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. It is normalized before being stored and
            returned: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and internal runs of whitespace
            collapsed to a single space, the value is upper-cased and common abbreviations are
            expanded as whole tokens (ST -> STREET, RD -> ROAD, AVE -> AVENUE). So
            '  12  main  st ' is stored and returned as '12 MAIN STREET'. An address that is
            blank after normalization is rejected with 400. Household duplicate detection and
            the shared household id both compare addresses in this normalized form.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The pet owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; validated only when present. When
            supplied it must be a valid postcode for the city's region per the fixed table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099), where the region is derived from
            the city (Sydney -> NSW, Melbourne -> VIC, Brisbane -> QLD). A postcode out of
            range for the city's region is rejected with 400. A city with no known region
            accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned as supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. It is normalized into E.164 form: a
            leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces,
            dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must contain 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. So '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'. The pattern
            tolerates an optional leading '+' plus digits and separators (spaces, brackets,
            dashes); numbers that cannot form valid E.164 are rejected with 400.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]+$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional, but when present it must be a
            syntactically valid email address. The value is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 3
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional on
            create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner already shares the
            same last name and address (compared case-insensitively, with runs of whitespace
            collapsed). When omitted or false, such a duplicate is rejected with 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

## Summary

I implemented rejection of a future `registrationDate` on owner creation, returning **400 Bad Request**, following the repo's existing `PostcodeValidator` / `InvalidPostcodeException` convention:

1. **`util/InvalidRegistrationDateException.java`** (new) — a `RuntimeException` thrown when the supplied registration date lies in the future, mirroring `InvalidPostcodeException`.

2. **`util/RegistrationDateValidator.java`** (new) — validates a supplied date, accepting `null` (which still defaults to the server date on persist via `Owner.onCreate()`) and throwing when `registrationDate.isAfter(LocalDate.now())`.

3. **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, calls `RegistrationDateValidator.validate(owner.getRegistrationDate())` right after the existing `PostcodeValidator.validate(...)`.

4. **`rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** — added an `@ExceptionHandler(InvalidRegistrationDateException.class)` that maps the exception to a 400 `ProblemDetail`, consistent with the telephone/postcode handlers.

The acceptance test `errorRejectsFutureDate` (posting `registrationDate: "2999-01-01"`) now gets a 400, and the validator leaves the common case (omitted/past date) untouched.
